key_insight: A shared tether tunes frequency splitting and dissipation in coupled square resonators, with short couplers enabling symmetric-mode dissipation dilution above the isolated-polygon value.
engineering_relevance: Coupler geometry offers a design lever for controlling mechanical coupling while reducing dissipation in resonator devices.
method: Develop a continuum model of two identical square resonators joined by a shared tether.
Relate coupler dimensions to mode splitting and dissipation dilution; compare predictions with finite element simulations.
Derive short-coupler and short-tether scaling for the quality-factor–frequency product, Q·f.
evidence_signal: For a 100 μm-long, 2 μm-wide coupler, finite element calculations yield 17.7 Hz frequency splitting and symmetric-mode dilution approximately 13% above the analytical isolated-polygon value.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based, and the simplified Q·f expression assumes short couplers and short supporting tethers.
paper_title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
